title: LINQ queries
description:
A shop's sales are records:

```csharp
public record Sale(string Product, string Region, decimal Price, int Quantity);
```

Answer these questions with LINQ (no loops), each as a method in `Solution`:

```csharp
public static decimal Revenue(IEnumerable<Sale> sales)                          // sum of Price * Quantity
public static List<string> TopProducts(IEnumerable<Sale> sales, int n)          // by total quantity, ties by name
public static Dictionary<string, decimal> RevenueByRegion(IEnumerable<Sale> sales)
public static string? BiggestSale(IEnumerable<Sale> sales)                     // "Product in Region" of the highest Price * Quantity, or null
public static List<string> RegionsSelling(IEnumerable<Sale> sales, string product)   // distinct regions, sorted
```
hints: `GroupBy(s => s.Product)` gives one group per product; `g.Sum(s => s.Quantity)` totals each group.
`MaxBy` returns `null` for an empty sequence of records, so `is Sale s` both checks and captures the result.
rules: Use LINQ instead of foreach loops.
Use LINQ instead of for loops.
